definition: The Identification and Referral to Improve Safety (IRIS)-embedded specialist domestic-abuse worker who delivers whole-practice training to a GP practice and provides one-to-one advocacy to patients. In Middlesbrough the role is based at My Sister's Place.
source: The Identification and Referral to Improve Safety (IRIS) programme, which defines the Advocate Educator (AE) role; delivered locally at My Sister's Place, Middlesbrough (the postholder holds the SafeLives Older Persons Violence Advisor qualification).

definition: The local delivery of Women's Aid's national 'Ask Me' community ambassador scheme (part of Change That Lasts), Middlesbrough Council-funded, training community members to recognise and signpost on domestic abuse.
source: Women's Aid — the national 'Ask Me' community ambassador scheme (part of Change That Lasts); delivered locally with Middlesbrough Council funding.

full_term: Child / Adolescent to Parent Violence and Abuse
definition: Abuse perpetrated by a child or adolescent against a parent or carer. Where those involved are both aged 16 or over it also falls within the statutory definition of domestic abuse (Domestic Abuse Act 2021, s.1).
source: Tees Child Protection Partnership — Child to Parent Violence and Abuse guidance; the national concept is set out in the Home Office (2015) Information guide: Adolescent to Parent Violence and Abuse

definition: The former county of Cleveland (1974–1996), created by the Local Government Act 1972 and abolished by the Cleveland (Structural Change) Order 1995, which replaced it with four unitary authorities — Middlesbrough, Redcar & Cleveland, Stockton-on-Tees and Hartlepool. The name survives in bodies whose footprint still covers that geography, notably Cleveland Police and its Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner (OPCC).
source: The Cleveland (Structural Change) Order 1995 (SI 1995/187), which abolished the county created by the Local Government Act 1972; the geography survives as the Cleveland Police / OPCC footprint.

full_term: Crime Survey for England and Wales
aliases: Crime Survey for England and Wales
definition: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) victimisation survey; nationally representative but not robust at local-authority level.
source: Crime Survey for England and Wales (Office for National Statistics) — a National Statistic governed by the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007

definition: An immediate, short-term notice issued directly by the police to give a victim of domestic abuse emergency protection.
source: Domestic Abuse Act 2021, Part 3

definition: A longer-term, flexible protective order granted by a court to protect a victim of domestic abuse.
source: Domestic Abuse Act 2021, Part 3

definition: Domestic Abuse Risk Assessment tool, developed by the College of Policing as the successor to Domestic Abuse, Stalking and Honour-Based Violence (DASH).
source: College of Policing — the Domestic Abuse Risk Assessment (DARA), which replaces DASH
org_ref: findthatcharity org ID GB-GOVUK-college-of-policing (College of Policing)

definition: The practice of routinely asking service users about domestic abuse, regardless of whether abuse is suspected.
source: Cleveland Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner — Decision Notice 2025-26-018: Domestic Abuse Routine Enquiry.

full_term: Domestic Abuse, Stalking and Honour-Based Violence
definition: The risk-assessment checklist formerly used by police and partners to identify high-risk domestic abuse cases; held by the College of Policing and since replaced by the Domestic Abuse Risk Assessment (DARA).
source: College of Policing — DASH risk assessment (now replaced by DARA)
org_ref: findthatcharity org ID GB-GOVUK-college-of-policing (College of Policing)

definition: Statutory multi-agency review after a death in which abuse is suspected.
source: Domestic Violence, Crime and Victims Act 2004, s.9

definition: Behaviour by a person towards another to whom they are personally connected, where both are aged 16 or over and the behaviour is abusive — physical or sexual abuse, violent or threatening behaviour, controlling or coercive behaviour, economic abuse, or psychological, emotional or other abuse.
source: Domestic Abuse Act 2021, s.1

definition: The role that delivers the programme's Enhanced Case Management workstream. Enhanced Case Workers support people who are already in the system, using a multi-agency 'team around the individual' approach, and reach out to people rather than waiting for referrals. It is a higher-intensity role than the Key Worker.
source: South Tees Delivery Plan (Version 2), Workstream 2 (Enhanced Case Management).

definition: Harbour Support Services — the specialist domestic-abuse charity delivering the Redcar & Cleveland model; with Changing Futures funding it hosts the GP Link Worker.
NHS England activity dataset; historically under-coded for domestic abuse.
source: NHS England / NHS Digital — Hospital Episode Statistics (HES)

definition: The statutory NHS body that plans and commissions health services for a defined area.
source: Health and Care Act 2022 (ICBs, Part 1)

definition: A specialist domestic-abuse support worker for survivors at high risk of harm.
source: SafeLives.

full_term: Identification and Referral to Improve Safety
definition: The evidence-based primary-care domestic-abuse training and referral programme developed by Gene Feder and colleagues at the University of Bristol; general practices are trained and given a direct referral pathway to a specialist advocate. National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)-endorsed; licensed and supported by the social enterprise IRISi.
source: Identification and Referral to Improve Safety (IRIS) — Feder et al. (2011), University of Bristol; NICE-endorsed; licensed by IRISi.

full_term: Identification and Referral to Improve Safety — extended version (children and men)
definition: An Identification and Referral to Improve Safety (IRIS) adaptation extending to men, children and perpetrators. Not delivered in Middlesbrough as of May 2026.
source: University of Bristol, Centre for Academic Primary Care (2024) — IRIS+ extends the health-care response (with IRISi)

definition: The statutory Health and Wellbeing Board discharging the section 194 duty jointly for Middlesbrough and Redcar & Cleveland; the political-level governance board for the joint South Tees Public Health function, co-chaired by the political leaders of the two authorities.
source: Health and Social Care Act 2012, s.194 (Health and Wellbeing Boards)

term: Live Well South Tees Executive Board
full_term: Live Well South Tees Executive Board
aliases: Live Well South Tees Executive Board
definition: The executive arm of the Live Well South Tees governance structure — the single forum where joint Public Health and each authority's Adult Social Care meet.
source: Executive arm of the Live Well South Tees Board (the statutory Health and Wellbeing Board, HSCA 2012 s.194); constituted by local terms of reference.

definition: The Harbour-employed GP Independent Domestic Violence Advocate / Advisor (IDVA) in Redcar & Cleveland. Dual-remit covering domestic abuse and substance use within the THRIVE partnership. 3.
source: Harbour — the GP-based Independent Domestic Violence Advocate role in Redcar & Cleveland, within the THRIVE partnership.

definition: The multi-agency forum for managing the highest-risk domestic abuse cases.
source: SafeLives — What is a MARAC? (SafeLives stewards the national MARAC model and holds the definition)

definition: A commissioned specialist domestic-abuse service in Middlesbrough; hosts the Identification and Referral to Improve Safety (IRIS) Advocate Educator.

full_term: NICE Public Health Guideline 50 (Domestic violence and abuse: multi-agency working)
definition: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Public Health Guideline 50, Domestic violence and abuse: multi-agency working (2014); names Identification and Referral to Improve Safety (IRIS) and concludes domestic-abuse interventions are broadly cost-effective.
source: NICE PH50 (2014), Domestic violence and abuse: multi-agency working

definition: An immigration condition that excludes a person from most welfare benefits and from statutory homelessness assistance; significant for some cohorts in Middlesbrough.
source: Immigration and Asylum Act 1999, s.115(9) (defines a person subject to immigration control, on condition of no recourse to public funds)

full_term: Office of the Police and Crime Commissioner
definition: The elected office responsible for the governance of policing in a force area — setting the police and crime plan and holding the Chief Constable to account; created by the Police Reform and Social Responsibility Act 2011.
source: Police Reform and Social Responsibility Act 2011

definition: Good-practice guidance on the health-service response to domestic abuse (Pathfinder Consortium, 2020), cited in the statutory guidance as good practice.
source: Pathfinder Consortium (2020).

definition: A group of neighbouring GP practices working together, sitting beneath the Integrated Care Board (ICB). Established in England from 2019/20 through the Network Contract Directed Enhanced Service (DES) under the GP contract, as set out in the NHS Long Term Plan.
source: Network Contract DES (NHS England, 2019/20), under the NHS Act 2006

definition: The comparative implementation-science framework (Glasgow, Vogt and Boles, 1999) used to structure the cross-cutting analysis.
source: Glasgow, Vogt and Boles (1999) — Reach, Effectiveness, Adoption, Implementation, Maintenance evaluation framework.

definition: Middlesbrough and Redcar & Cleveland together — the two-local-authority geography of the South Tees Changing Futures Programme. Distinct from Cleveland.
source: South Tees Changing Futures programme geography; BRAND.md §4.

definition: All the services around a person — health, housing, social care, justice, substance use, domestic abuse and welfare, whether statutory, commissioned or voluntary-sector — seen from the person's point of view rather than any one agency's. The related principle is that the system should adapt to the person, not the person to the system.
source: Working definition adopted in this deep-dive series.

definition: The Redcar and Cleveland partnership delivering England's first integrated Domestic Abuse and Substance Use (IDAS) service model: collaborative, trauma-informed support. THRIVE stands for Trusting, Hopeful, Resilient, Involved, Valued and Empowered. Partners: We Are With You (drug and alcohol support), Redcar and Cleveland Borough Council, Harbour Support Services (domestic abuse), Recovery Connections and Intuitive Thinking Skills.
source: We Are With You — the Thrive Partnership (Redcar and Cleveland; England's first integrated Domestic Abuse and Substance Use model); Thrive Impact Report 2024–2025

full_term: Voluntary, Community, Faith and Social Enterprise
aliases: voluntary, community, faith and social enterprise
definition: The sector Redcar and Cleveland Voluntary Development Agency (RCVDA) works within and holds the deep-dive work on behalf of.
source: Sector-standard term.

definition: Creates a statutory duty for local authorities, OPCCs and ICBs to collaborate on commissioning Domestic abuse (DA), sexual abuse and serious violence support, from April 2026.
source: Victims and Prisoners Act 2024

definition: We Are With You (formerly Addaction) — the commissioned substance-use service across Redcar & Cleveland.

The operating name since 2019 of the Big Lottery Fund: the UK's largest funder of community activity, distributing money raised for good causes by National Lottery players. Joint funder of Changing Futures with MHCLG.
source: National Lottery Act 2006 (established the Big Lottery Fund, which has operated as The National Lottery Community Fund since 2019).

definition: National domestic-abuse charity that develops and stewards the evidence base and models for the high-risk response, including the Multi-Agency Risk Assessment Conference (MARAC) and the Independent Domestic Violence Advisor (IDVA) models. Known as Co-ordinated Action Against Domestic Abuse (CAADA) until it was renamed SafeLives in 2014.
source: SafeLives — Our history
